summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for SSH key-only access: created the user, installed the specified ed25519 public key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct permissions, locked the account password, and enforced key-based SSH authentication cluster-wide via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf (PasswordAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes, PermitEmptyPasswords no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no). Also had to generate missing SSH host keys and fix the missing /run/sshd privilege-separation directory (added a systemd-tmpfiles rule so it persists across reboots) since sshd was not actually running beforehand. Verified end-to-end with real SSH logins (password auth rejected, pubkey auth succeeds). Completed the mandatory node1 restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id and service state, issued a native reboot, polled until the node returned, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd, opsadmin, the authorized key, and functional key-based login all recovered correctly post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: no opsadmin user, sshd_config default, no host keys, ssh.service not actually running
Installed required ed25519 public key into /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with 700/600 perms and correct ownership
Locked opsadmin's password (passwd -l) to remove password-login option for the account

Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf enforcing PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / PermitEmptyPasswords no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no / ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
Generated missing SSH host keys via ssh-keygen -A
Created missing /run/sshd directory and added /etc/tmpfiles.d/sshd.conf to recreate it on boot
Started and enabled ssh.service and ssh.socket
Verified effective sshd config via sshd -T
Functionally tested SSH: password auth rejected (Permission denied publickey), pubkey auth via a temporary test key succeeded, then removed the temporary key leaving only the required key

Executed mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id and service/config state, issued `sudo reboot` via nohup/background so acknowledgement returned first, polled node1 until reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed, re-verified sshd active, key-only policy in effect, opsadmin and authorized_keys intact, and re-ran a live SSH pubkey login test post-reboot to confirm recovery

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user created with the specified public key installed for SSH access
evidence.summary: useradd creates opsadmin (uid 1000); authorized_keys populated with exactly the required ed25519 key with correct ownership/permissions

evidence.requirement: SSH requires key-based authentication (password auth disabled)
evidence.summary: sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf written and passes sshd -t; effective config (sshd -T) shows pubkeyauthentication yes / passwordauthentication no / permitemptypasswords no; live SSH attempt restricted to password auth is rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)'

evidence.requirement: Key-based SSH login actually functions for opsadmin
evidence.summary: SSH login using a temporary ed25519 key added to authorized_keys succeeds (whoami=opsadmin, LOGIN_OK), proving the pubkey auth path works end-to-end; temp key was removed afterward leaving only the required key (cmd-2473e1a7cf284871)
Captured boot_id 4d70780a-0bff-4d50-8c53-62faa1ccc945, ssh.service active, key-only sshd policy, opsadmin user and authorized_keys all healthy prior to restart
`sudo reboot` issued via backgrounded nohup; command returned 'reboot issued, pid 1848' immediately

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just service restart)
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable (connection timed out) immediately after reboot, then came back with a new boot_id 9a2a77b3-d923-483b-82bf-53abb5ac9502 (differs from baseline 4d70780a...) and uptime 0 min

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, ssh.service active, key-only auth policy intact, opsadmin user and correct authorized_keys entry present, /run/sshd recreated by tmpfiles rule, and a live SSH pubkey login test succeeded (LOGIN_OK_POSTREBOOT), confirming full functional recovery
